svg.title: Minor sixth versus major sixth
svg.desc: Minor sixth versus major sixth. A keyboard from C4 to C5 with C4 as the shared root and the upper notes A♭4 (m6, 8 semitones), A4 (M6, 9 semitones) each in its own identity colour. A table lists what stayed (root C4) and what changed (upper note, semitone count, and the Plogger shape, shadow and fill where they apply).

g.text: C4 to A♭4 (8) and C4 to A4 (9).
m6 → M6: +1 semitone on the upper note
HOW TO READ THE THREE PLOGGER MARKS
A Shape (outline): jagged = dissonant family · rounded = modal family · straight = perfect-group
family. A family label, not a measured sound wave.
B Shadow (side): ← Fundamental [1]–[5] · ↔ Both [6] · → Octave [7]–[11]. Always paired with its
C Fill (inside): dense/dark = non-harmonic · open/light = harmonic · midtone dotted = neutral [6]
A historic teaching lens from the archived printed Plogger di-chord pictograph, not acoustic law.
The identity colour is a separate, artistic label.
